I have 6.37 hectares here in Tabora, and the land is my own. I grow my crops mixed together — maybe some maize with cassava, the way we do here — because if one fails the other carries us. Cash is tight and fertilizer in Tabora is expensive to bring from town, so I do not buy it; I rely on what the soil gives and on rotating where I plant. For seed I keep what I harvested last year, same as my neighbors, and I use my hand-hoe with my family and hire a few young men at weeding time because 6 hectares is too much for us alone.
